title: Action Model
description:
A named, declarative behaviour a page can perform. Actions are the platform's only mechanism for anything to happen: components emit events, pages map events to actions, and the runtime executes them. Keeping behaviour declarative is what makes interaction generatable by the AI and analysable by the renderer — interaction expressed in component code would be permanently outside both.

This model also carries the forward seam for write-back (v2) and workflow (v3). Those kinds are defined here, deliberately, so that adding them later is additive rather than a breaking change to a schema that thousands of stored definitions conform to. They are marked reserved and rejected by the v1 platform validator.

confirm.description: Confirmation prompt shown before execution. Required by validation for any action with side effects.

requiresReason.description: Prompt for a free-text reason recorded in the audit trail — the norm for data overrides in a governed environment.

auditProfile.description: 'elevated' forces an audit record even for read-only actions. Applied to export and to anything that moves data outside the platform.

navigateAction.description: Move to another page or experience, mapping parameters explicitly.

tab.description: Deep-link a specific tab of the target page.

params.description: Target parameter values. Values typically come from the triggering event payload via $context, e.g. { "securityId": { "$context": "$event.securityId" } }.

carryContext.description: Carry experience-scoped parameters through, so an as-of date chosen on a dashboard survives a drill into detail. Without this, every drill-down silently resets shared context.

drilldownAction.description: Navigate into an instance of a catalog entity without naming a target page. The target resolves from the entity's defaultDetailExperience, and key parameters are derived from the entity's primaryKey. This is the generic form: any component bound to an entity can offer drill-down, every page drills to the same place, and the AI does not have to know the page graph to generate a working drill-through.

key.description: Primary key values, keyed by the entity's primaryKey attribute ids. Omitted means take them from the triggering event payload by matching names.

targetOverride.description: Explicit target, overriding the entity default. Present as an escape hatch; using it forfeits the consistency the generic form provides.

setFilterAction.description: Write to a shared filter channel. The declarative form of cross-widget filtering: clicking a chart segment filters the grid beside it.

channels.description: Omitted clears every channel on the page.

updateUrl.description: Reflect the change in the URL so the resulting view is shareable and bookmarkable.

dataSources.description: Omitted refreshes every source on the page.

exportAction.description: Export data. Governed as a data egress event: the export carries the exporter's entitlements, is audited, and is subject to tenant export policy. Every other control in the platform applies to data on a screen; a spreadsheet leaves the perimeter entirely.

scope.description: 'view' exports what is displayed; 'all' re-queries without paging, subject to the export row limit.

includeMetadata.description: Stamp the export with as-of date, filters applied, user and timestamp. Strongly recommended: an undated extract of governed data is a compliance liability.

openUrlAction.description: Open an external URL. The template is restricted to declared parameters and cannot be assembled from arbitrary data, which prevents a definition being used to build an exfiltration endpoint.

openOverlayAction.description: Open a drawer or modal declared in the page layout, without navigating.

compositeAction.description: Ordered sequence of other actions — set a filter, then refresh, then open a drawer. Sequencing is explicit rather than emergent, so behaviour is predictable and reviewable.

invokeAction.description: RESERVED — v2 write-back. Invokes a governed platform operation that mutates EDM data: an override, a correction, an approval, a bulk update. Defined now so that the seam exists: adding write-back later becomes a new action kind plus an operation registry, not a breaking change to the action model. The v1 platform validator rejects this kind.

operation.description: Operation id from the governed operation registry. Operations are server-defined and entitlement-checked; a definition can only ever reference one, never describe one.

targetSelection.description: Selection channel supplying the rows to act on, for bulk operations.

idempotencyKeyFrom.description: Expression producing a stable idempotency key, so a retried invocation cannot double-apply.

optimisticConcurrency.description: Field carrying the row version the user saw. Required for safe concurrent editing of governed data.

workflowAction.description: RESERVED — v3 workflow. Interacts with a workflow instance: start a process, complete a task, approve, reject, reassign, escalate. Present as a seam only. Workflow is a distinct product surface with its own definition schema — state machines, task assignment, SLAs, escalation, compensation — and is deliberately not modelled here; what is modelled is the point at which a page touches it. The v1 platform validator rejects this kind.

taskRef.description: Task instance, for task operations. Normally bound from a selection channel over a task queue.
